messages:
michael: quick heads-up — ran a 2h sampling job on canary to isolate TTFT spikes vs decode kernel time. noticed high variance on certain routes

tara: nice, which routes? any correlation with batch sizes or kv cache hit rate? :chart_with_upwards_trend:

michael: mostly /chat and /summarize. batch size distribution shifted to right (more 8-16 microbatches) on the noisy routes. kvcache hit rate dropped ~7% on those samples

aj: do you have examples of the kernel attribution traces? i want to see prequeue vs kernel handoff times

michael: pasted a trimmed export from the probe:
```
trace_id=64812 route=/chat seq_len=512 batch=12
metrics: ttft_ms=48.3 decode_ms=31.1 prequeue_ms=10.2 kernel_handoff_ms=6.4
kernels: matmul_ms=12.3 attention_ms=9.6 postproc_ms=1.8 other_ms=7.4
kvcache: hit=false lookup_ms=0.6 evict=false
```

sophia: hmm decode_ms accounts for ~65% of ttft in that sample. but kernel handoff and prequeue still non-trivial. could be a scheduler backpressure issue when batch sizes jump

aj: agree. i also pulled per-request router logs: we see small bursts where scheduling delay spikes to 15-25ms when many concurrent short requests land. our batching heuristic currently favors joining open microbatches for 25ms window

tara: could the batching window be too aggressive for the /summarize route? those requests are short but latency-sensitive. maybe we should stratify batch windows by route SLA

michael: here's a quick diff of a probe config i tried locally (only for canary):
```json
{"heuristics": {"default_window_ms": 25, "route_overrides": {"/summarize": {"window_ms": 10, "min_batch": 1}}}
```

sophia: interesting, did that reduce prequeue_ms?

michael: yes, median prequeue dropped from 10.2 -> 4.1 on /summarize, but microbatch throughput fell 8% and token cost up slightly. TTFT median improved ~6% for that route

aj: tradeoff expected. important to tie this to per-route KPIs in dashboard so product teams can choose cost vs latency

michael: on kvcache side i saw a pattern where evictions surged right before spikes. looks like our kvcache LRU bucket size is thrashing under wide seq_len variance

tara: can you share the eviction timeline? we want an alert if eviction_rate > 0.1%/min on a route during canary

michael: log snippet: 
```
2026-11-02T14:12:01Z route=/chat evictions=3 total_entries=2400 eviction_rate=0.125%
2026-11-02T14:12:11Z route=/chat evictions=9 total_entries=2402 eviction_rate=0.375%
```

sophia: that matches the KV hotset mismatch hypothesis. prefetching smaller prefixes for long sequences might help reduce lookup latency when hitting cold entries

aj: also worth instrumenting kernel selector decisions per-token so we can attribute which kernel was chosen and why. i want a small panel: kernel_choice, input_len, kv_hit, chosen_cuda_kernel, fallback_reason

tara: +1. and add percentiles for ttft vs decode in the per-route overview. ops asked for p50/p90/p99 split across kernel-choice buckets

michael: created a short dashboard proto on Grafana (canary workspace) with three panels: 1) TTFT vs decode time series by route, 2) kernel choice distribution heatmap, 3) kvcache hit/miss + eviction timeline. pinned it to #eng-runtime for early eyeballs

sophia: can you drop the dashboard link? i'll run an eval suite against it tomorrow morning and check regressions

michael: link: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/canary/ttft-kernel-probe (note: access restricted)

aj: next steps i propose:
- add kernel_choice tagging to sampling exporter (low-overhead flags)
- route-aware batching window experiment for /summarize and /chat (A/B)
- kvcache eviction alert + prefetch experiment on canary

michael: added an RFC-lite in the perf tracker: https://go/internal/notes/ttft-kernel-handoff (contains config, experiment plan, and rollback criteria)

tara: on the alerting side, ops wants to see a combined signal: ttft_p90 rise AND kvcache_eviction_rate rising for 2 consecutive minutes before firing. avoids noisy single-metric flips

sophia: i'll own the A/B run and send a short summary after 6h window. planning to capture token-level traces for 1% sample rate

devbot: deployment: canary config updated by michael at 1988887825. rolling update started. :gear:

michael: thanks — i'll follow up with a short writeup and attach the raw probe exports. if anyone wants the raw traces sooner ping me directly

aj: perfect. if the kernel attribution panel shows a consistent non-kernel decode component, we should spike a small optimization ticket to look at attention kernel memory copies

tara: noted. tagging infra and eng-runtime owners in the RFC. :white_check_mark:

sophia: thanks everyone — excited to see if per-route windows give a clean win

michael: :thumbsup:
